deities: Lord Bharata (presiding deity; 179 cm standing sila idol, four-armed with bow, abhaya, chakra and conch; sankalpam of Bharata worshipping Lord Rama's padukas)
Goddess Durga and Sree Bhadrakali (mural paintings on the agra-mandapam pillars)
festivals: Koodalmanikyam Utsavam / Arattu (10-11 days in Medam/Edavam, April-May; begins one day after Thrissur Pooram and ends on the next Thiruvonam; 17 caparisoned elephants, seven with gold Nettipattam)
Thriputhari (Thiruvonam nakshatra in Thulam, October-November; newly harvested rice offered, followed by the Mukkudi ayurvedic medicine offering)
Nalambalam Yatra (Karkidakam, July-August; the four-temple pilgrimage to Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna shrines)

history.dynasty: Chera (Kulasekhara) period origins; Thachuda Kaimal administration (from 1341 AD); Travancore mel-koyma (from 1746); Kerala Government takeover 1971
history.period: Ancient; earliest inscription c. 854 CE (11th regnal year of Chera king Stanu Ravi Varman)
history.summary: The Koodalmanikyam Temple at Irinjalakuda is the only major temple in India dedicated to Lord Bharata, the brother of Rama, and is one of the four Nalambalam temples of Kerala (Rama at Triprayar, Bharata at Irinjalakuda, Lakshmana at Moozhikkulam, Shatrughna at Payammal). The earliest historical reference is a stone inscription of the Chera king Stanu Ravi Varman dated c. 854 CE recording a land donation, though the shrine is clearly older and Irinjalakuda was one of the 64 ancient gramams of Kerala. Legends give the temple several origin stories: Vakkayil Kaimal's dream of four Vishnu idols washed ashore near Triprayar (which became the Nalambalam set); the 'koodal-manikyam' (merging of the gem) story of 1341 AD that brought Thachuda Kaimal administration; and the conch-shattering legend behind the Lord's name Sangameswaran (holder of unified Shaivite and Vaishnavite powers). The temple was damaged in Tippu Sultan's 1789 invasion and renovated by Shaktan Thampuran, and was taken over by the Kerala Government under the Koodalmanikyam Temple Act of 1971. It is famous for its distinctive customs: no Balikkalppura, no sreebali and no deeparadhana, with three daily poojas instead of the usual five.

name: Koodalmanikyam Temple
town_description: Irinjalakuda is a municipal town in Thrissur district, about 25 km south of Thrissur city, and was one of the 64 ancient Brahmin gramams of Kerala. It is best known as the seat of the Koodalmanikyam Bharata temple, which historically owned vast lands in and around the town. The town is also a gateway stop on the Nalambalam pilgrimage circuit and lies near the Chalakudy and Kurumali river belt.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (COK), Nedumbassery (approx. 37-39 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Irinjalakuda Railway Station (approx. 7-9 km; sources vary); Thrissur Railway Station (approx. 20-22 km) is the major railhead.
travel.road: The temple is about 1 km from the Irinjalakuda Municipal Bus Stand (150 m from the old stand area per local guides); KSRTC and private buses connect Irinjalakuda with Thrissur (approx. 1 hour), Kodungallur and Chalakudy. Auto-rickshaws are readily available within town.

visitor_information.best_time: Throughout the year; April-May for the grand 10-11-day annual Utsavam/Arattu (starts a day after Thrissur Pooram); October-November for Thriputhari; July-August for the Nalambalam pilgrimage season. Weekday mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning approx. 3:00 AM to 11:30 AM; evening approx. 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM (sources vary slightly on the opening time — 3:00, 3:30 or 4:00 AM reported; the detailed schedule is 4:00 AM darshan, 7:30 AM ethirthu-pooja, 11:00 AM uccha-pooja, 7:45 PM athazha-pooja). Traditional attire recommended; footwear not allowed inside.
